subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by landing the shared fenced reply-session-init self-heal first, by adding explicit inbound retry parity for the transient-drop paths, or by moving the root fix to an `acquireSessionWriteLock`-style serialization boundary?
rationale: The source and field evidence show a real message-loss/session-state bug, but maintainers must choose the permanent owner boundary because the open shared PR and the newer comments cover overlapping but not identical failure modes.

options.title: Choose Shared Root Serialization
options.body: Treat the central reply-session init path as the owner and implement or land a shared fix that prevents ordinary same-session CAS races before adding per-channel retries.

options.title: Land Self-Heal Then Retest
options.body: Review and land the open self-heal PR first, then require focused proof for the transient WebChat, heartbeat, Discord, Signal, WhatsApp, and Slack drop cases before closing this issue.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Keep the shared self-heal separate and require explicit retry/spool behavior in each affected inbound path, accepting the ongoing parity-maintenance cost.

recommendation.title: Choose Shared Root Serialization
recommendation.body: Treat the central reply-session init path as the owner and implement or land a shared fix that prevents ordinary same-session CAS races before adding per-channel retries.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest recent merged history on the guarded reply-session initialization and session-accessor boundary where the owner decision sits.
